summary: Three trade blocs share one shipping lane and no referee. Tariffs are the weapon, the strait is the chokepoint, and every season somebody discovers what their neighbours were willing to do.
audience_tone: Dry, procedural, faintly amused. Economics reported like a blood sport, and nobody in the room admits it is one.

characters.name: Chancellor Ferrox
characters.title: Chancellor of the Ironbelt
characters.brief: Runs the furnaces, the foundries and the political careers attached to them. Believes a bloc that imports its own steel has already surrendered and simply has not been told. Reads every concession as a debt someone will collect later.
goals: Keep the grain duty and make the Sunbelt say it is fair
Get the strait toll rolled back without asking Okuma for anything
Never be seen to need a neighbour
taboos: Never negotiates in private what could be announced

characters.name: Premier Cindra
characters.title: Premier of the Compact
characters.brief: Grain, sun and patience. Feeds half the map and is careful that everyone can see her doing it. Her generosity is real and it is also a ledger, and she has never pretended otherwise to anyone who asked.
goals: Break the grain duty publicly rather than quietly
Keep the Ironbelt tenements fed and keep the receipts
taboos: Never lets a shipment be turned away
Never raises her voice in session
Never takes a side she cannot walk back out of

characters.name: Director Okuma
characters.title: Director of the Exchange
characters.brief: Owns no fields and no furnaces, only the water between them, which has always been enough. Sets the strait toll on a schedule nobody else is shown and calls every use of it routine.
goals: Be indispensable to both of them and loyal to neither
Never let the blocs settle directly
taboos: Never closes the strait for a stated reason
Never appears at a summit uninvited

tics: gives a schedule instead of an answer

relationships.note: She feeds my tenements so my own people will look at her when they are hungry.
He put a duty on food and called it a correction.
He raised the toll the day my convoys were due and called it routine.
He shouts at water. The water does not move.
Useful, and I have not yet had to find out what it costs.
She pays on time and asks for nothing, which is its own kind of pressure.

arcs.title: The Grain Duty
arcs.summary: The Ironbelt put a 40% duty on Sunbelt grain and called it a correction. The Compact has not retaliated and has not stopped shipping, which is worse.

arcs.title: The Strait Toll
arcs.summary: The Exchange raised the toll on a schedule it will not publish, on the day the ore convoys were due. Everyone agrees it was routine.

tone.register: Dry procedural economics played as a blood sport. People talk about tonnage, schedules and duties. Nobody explains the game and nobody addresses the camera.
